builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
summary: Veritas replaces hand-written task verifiers with automatically generated ones, using an evidence header, a domain-rule library, and authoring principles refined by a self-improvement loop. The cost is additional LLM calls for verifier generation plus maintaining the rule library and generation pipeline, and gains are measured as agreement with official verdicts rather than end-task quality. It can fail where generated verifiers encode incorrect or incomplete domain rules, where agreement with official benchmarks does not transfer to the reader's own tasks, or where self-improvement refinement drifts without ground-truth checks.
rationale: The method is implementable with API access and directly addresses verifier scarcity in self-improving agent loops, but its agreement-based gains require validation on the reader's own tasks before production reliance.
technique: Automatic verifier generation for agent tasks

claims.statement: Veritas replaces hand-written task verifiers with automatically generated ones, using an evidence header, a domain-rule library, and authoring principles refined by a self-improvement loop. The cost is additional LLM calls for verifier generation plus maintaining the rule library and generation pipeline, and gains are measured as agreement with official verdicts rather than end-task quality. It can fail where generated verifiers encode incorrect or incomplete domain rules, where agreement with official benchmarks does not transfer to the reader's own tasks, or where self-improvement refinement drifts without ground-truth checks.

Generated verifiers agree better with official verdicts than seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks (model fixed), and are at or near best on two pairwise benchmarks; mechanisms improve 9 of 12 harness-benchmark pairs across three harnesses.
